rows.notes: The document is explicitly a review paper (CABI/STFC report 'Review paper: Pests, diseases and invasive species') synthesising literature, policy documents and a stakeholder workshop. It contains no own field, laboratory, survey or validated model result on spectral/thermal early stress detection reducing prophylactic pesticide applications. The only primary-like elements are a Web of Science/CABDirect bibliometric count, a stakeholder workshop listing stressors and data needs (Tables 3 and 6), and brief mentions of pilot studies on irrigation datasets and M. acridum efficacy mapping, none of which address the claimed effect. Statements about remote sensing enabling targeted pest management (e.g. Table 3 'Improvements in precision agriculture techniques... lower environmental impact', section 3.0 on hyperspectral/thermal early detection of Xylella) are cited from other work (Poblete et al. 2020, Hornero et al. 2020, Zhang et al. 2020) or are workshop opinion, and the report itself notes that such detection has mostly been demonstrated at leaf/canopy/small-plot scale. Early detection is at most a precondition of reduced pesticide use; no reduction in applications is reported.
